name: XTAL Search for WooCommerce
author: XTAL Search

sections.description:
XTAL Search connects WooCommerce to the hosted XTAL Search service. It syncs your catalog and ranks product results for natural-language searches while continuing to use your theme’s WooCommerce templates.

Features:

  • Natural-language search – Handles queries such as “comfortable shoes for running”
  • Catalog sync – Sends product changes to XTAL as they are published
  • Theme-native results – Uses your existing WooCommerce product templates
  • Native fallback – Uses WooCommerce search when the XTAL API is unavailable
  • Safe rollout – Enable or disable XTAL at any time. XTAL can run a rollout test on your store: a set share of visitors (for example half) sees XTAL Search while the rest keep the store’s built-in search, and search, click, add-to-cart, and order events are reported for both groups so the two can be compared before you commit. The share in use is shown on the settings page while a test runs.

How It Works:

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In the plugin settings, open the signup link next to API Key. The link carries this installation’s random site ID so XTAL creates the correct store and collection.
  3. Complete signup and follow the emailed invite to generate and copy your API key.
  4. Paste the key, enable XTAL Search, and save the settings.
  5. Email hello@xtalsearch.com when the status panel asks you to activate the account.
  6. After XTAL confirms activation, run the first catalog sync.
  7. Product search pages use XTAL’s ranking and your theme’s WooCommerce templates.

External Service Connection

This plugin connects to the XTAL Search service at api2.xtalsearch.com. Activating the plugin alone does not contact XTAL. Opening the account signup link sends a random installation identifier (site_uuid) and the value platform=woocommerce to XTAL. Saving an API key sends the key to XTAL for validation and connection status. When XTAL Search is enabled, the plugin fetches its search configuration from XTAL about once a minute (sending only the API key) and can send the service data listed below.

Data transmitted to xtalsearch.com:

  • Product information (titles, descriptions, prices, images, SKUs, categories, tags, brand, variants, stock status, and product page links)
  • Product dimensions and weight, when set on the product, with their unit (for example “15.75 x 9.75 x 9.75 in”)
  • Every product attribute (taxonomy and custom, shown or hidden on the product page) as a label and its value(s)
  • Any additional product field you list under Extra fields to send to XTAL in the plugin settings (a custom field or an attribute/taxonomy value from that product), sent under the name you listed
  • The values of any fields you list under Fields customers search as codes in the plugin settings, sent as SKUs so a shopper who types the exact code gets an exact match
  • The XTAL API key, used to authenticate the store
  • A random WordPress installation identifier (site_uuid), used during signup to create the correct store and collection
  • Search queries entered by customers on your store
  • Search result interactions, including product clicks, result positions, and add-to-cart actions
  • Completed order events used for search attribution: order ID, total, currency, line items, and the searches attributed to those items
  • A pseudonymous session identifier stored in the xtal_sid cookie, used to connect searches with later clicks or purchases
  • A pseudonymous visitor identifier stored in the _xtal_vid cookie, used to keep a visitor on the same search variant during a rollout test
  • During a rollout test, the test identifier and which search variant the visitor saw, on search, click, add-to-cart and order events (order events carry the order ID, total, and currency)
  • Your web server’s IP address, which XTAL sees on every request (for rate limiting and abuse prevention)

Shoppers’ browsers never contact XTAL. The storefront script sends search, click, and add-to-cart events to your own site, which forwards them to XTAL with your API key. Order events are sent from your site’s server the same way. Search queries and Load More requests also go through your site.

The plugin does not send customer names, email addresses, postal addresses, payment details, IP addresses of shoppers, or WordPress account data. Your server’s IP address is processed transiently for rate limiting and abuse prevention and is not stored.

Cookies and browser storage set on your storefront:

  • xtal_sid (cookie, 30 days): a random session identifier, set by the storefront script, used to connect searches with later clicks or purchases. Not linked to a customer account.
  • _xtal_vid (cookie, 30 days, renewed on each visit): a random visitor identifier, set by the plugin on storefront pages whenever XTAL Search is enabled, used to keep a visitor in the same search variant for the length of a rollout test. Not linked to a customer account.
  • xtal:exposed (browser local storage): the current test identifier and session identifier, written once a visitor’s session has been reported as part of a rollout test so it is not reported twice from another tab.
  • xtal_recent_search and xtal_cart_attribution (browser session storage, cleared when the tab closes): the most recent XTAL search in this tab and which of its results were added to the cart, used to connect purchases with the search that led to them.

While XTAL Search is enabled, search, click, add-to-cart, and order events are also reported for visitors who see the store’s built-in search during a rollout test, so the two groups can be compared. Disabling XTAL Search stops catalog syncs, takes your store out of any rollout test (every visitor sees the store’s built-in search), stops all storefront search, click, add-to-cart, and order events, and sets no cookies. Saving an API key still performs a connection check.

Pricing:

XTAL Search is a paid hosted service. Start with the signup link next to API Key in the plugin settings, then follow the emailed invite to generate your key. Paste the key, enable XTAL Search, and save; then email hello@xtalsearch.com to activate your store. See xtalsearch.com/pricing for current rates.

  • Product Terms
  • Privacy Policy

Support

Email hello@xtalsearch.com or visit our Help Center.

Privacy

When XTAL Search is enabled, the plugin sends product data and storefront search queries to xtalsearch.com. It also sends product clicks, result positions, add-to-cart actions, and completed order events containing order ID, total, currency, and line items. These events measure search attribution. During a rollout test, these events also carry the test identifier and which search variant the visitor saw, and they are reported for visitors who see the store’s built-in search as well as for visitors who see XTAL Search.

Events use two random identifiers: a session identifier stored in the xtal_sid cookie and a visitor identifier stored in the _xtal_vid cookie, each kept for 30 days. The browser’s local storage holds xtal:exposed (the current test and session identifiers) and its session storage holds xtal_recent_search and xtal_cart_attribution (the most recent search in the tab and the results added to the cart from it). None of these is linked to a customer account. Shoppers’ browsers never contact XTAL: events go to your own site, which forwards them to XTAL with your API key. The plugin does not send customer names, email addresses, postal addresses, payment details, shoppers’ IP addresses, or WordPress account data. Your server’s IP address is processed transiently for rate limiting and abuse prevention and is not stored.

For detailed information about data handling, please see:
* XTAL Search Privacy Policy
* Product Terms

The plugin registers privacy policy content with WordPress, which you can view and include in your site’s privacy policy at Settings → Privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate XTAL Search from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Integrations → XTAL Search.
  3. Open the signup link next to API Key, complete signup, and follow the emailed link to copy your key.
  4. Paste the key, enable XTAL Search, and save the settings.
  5. When the status panel prompts you, email hello@xtalsearch.com to activate your store.
  6. After activation, run the initial catalog sync.
sections.faq:
Do I need an XTAL Search account?

Yes. Start with the signup link next to API Key in the plugin settings. It carries this installation’s random site ID. Complete signup, follow the emailed invite to generate your key, paste the key, enable XTAL Search, and save; then email hello@xtalsearch.com to activate the store.

What happens if the XTAL Search API is unavailable?

The plugin uses native WooCommerce product search until the XTAL API is available again.

Does this plugin work with my theme?

XTAL Search renders results through WooCommerce product templates so they follow the active theme.

How often are products synced?

Published product changes are synced as they occur. A scheduled full sync, daily by default, catches changes missed by those updates.

Is my customer data safe?

The plugin does not send customer names, email addresses, postal addresses, payment details, or WordPress account data. It sends catalog data, search queries, search interaction events, completed order events, pseudonymous session and visitor identifiers, and your web server’s IP address, as described under “External Service Connection.” Shoppers’ browsers never contact XTAL directly. See our Privacy Policy for details.

Why do some visitors see the store’s built-in search?

Your store is in a rollout test. While one runs, a set share of visitors sees XTAL Search and the rest keep the store’s built-in search, so the two can be compared on the same traffic. Each visitor stays in the same group for the length of the test. The share in use is shown on the plugin settings page while the test runs. Email hello@xtalsearch.com to change or end a test.

How many search results show per page?

Search results per page is set by Settings → Reading → “Blog pages show at most” in wp-admin, the same setting that controls how many posts show on your blog and archive pages. Your theme’s own “products per page” setting does not apply to XTAL search results. The current value is shown read-only on the XTAL Search settings page. When more results exist, a Load More button under the results fetches the next page.

Can I send XTAL product details that WooCommerce doesn’t store in a standard field?

Yes. Under WooCommerce → Settings → Integrations → XTAL Search, list custom field or attribute/taxonomy names, one per line, in Extra fields to send to XTAL. Each one is read from every product and sent to XTAL with its value. List field names in Fields customers search as codes to have their values treated like SKUs, so a shopper who types an exact code, such as an item number, gets an exact match. Only fields you list are sent beyond the plugin’s standard product data, which always includes built-in dimensions, weight, and every product attribute. The next sync sends the new fields; click Sync Now to send them right away.

Can a developer change the product data sent to XTAL?

Yes. The xtal_search_product_payload filter runs for every product on every sync, just before the product is sent. It receives the payload array and the WC_Product, and must return the payload. See docs/settings-reference.md in the plugin for the payload fields and a worked example.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Product sync sends each product’s dimensions, weight, and every attribute, including attributes hidden from the product page
  • New settings: “Extra fields to send to XTAL” sends custom fields you list, and “Fields customers search as codes” lets shoppers find a product by an exact code such as an item number. Saving a change starts a full sync
  • New xtal_search_product_payload filter lets developers add to the product data sent to XTAL
  • The search results heading shows a true count: “12 results for …” when every match fits on the first page, or “First 24 results for …” when more follow. WooCommerce’s “Showing N results” line, which always repeated the page size, is hidden on XTAL results pages
  • Load More appears only when more results exist, and advances correctly when the store carries only part of its XTAL catalog
  • The settings page shows how many search results appear per page and links to the setting that controls it
  • Search, click, and add-to-cart events now go from the shopper’s browser to your own site, which forwards them to XTAL with your API key; order events are sent with the key too. Shoppers’ browsers no longer contact XTAL
  • Search pages that fall back to WooCommerce’s own search are never page-cached, nginx FastCGI caches included, so XTAL results return as soon as XTAL is available
  • Rollout tests: XTAL can show XTAL Search to a set share of visitors while the rest keep the store’s built-in search; the share in use is shown read-only on the settings page while a test runs
  • New _xtal_vid cookie (random visitor identifier, 30 days, renewed on each visit) keeps a visitor in the same search variant; new browser storage key xtal:exposed marks a session as already reported
  • Search, click, add-to-cart, and order events carry the test identifier and which search variant the visitor saw, and are reported for visitors on the store’s built-in search during a test
  • Search results pages skip page caches, nginx FastCGI caches included, while a test runs
  • The plugin fetches its search configuration from XTAL about once a minute while enabled

1.0.1

  • WooCommerce’s result count now reports the XTAL total (“Showing 1-10 of 40 results”) instead of the current page size
  • Native paged search URLs (?paged=2) render the next slice of XTAL results instead of a 404
  • Load More resumes after the page that was rendered

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Semantic product search
  • Real-time product sync
  • Fallback to native WooCommerce search
  • Suggested privacy-policy text for WordPress
